tasks.title: Per-host rate limiting (ADR-034): the config key ADR-029 deferred is now enforced
tasks.notes: Lives in engine/, NOT core/policy: a limiter needs a clock and mutable state and core/ may have neither (test_architecture.py). Monotonic not wall-clock (a clock jump would bypass or lock out); sliding not fixed window (a fixed one admits 2x the rate across the boundary -- reproduced as a negative control that admits 6 where this admits 3); bounded host table that FAILS CLOSED (LIMITER_SATURATED) because evicting a live host would reset its budget and make the memory cap a bypass. check() and consume() are separate so a refusal elsewhere does not spend the host's budget. Host identity de-duplicated into core canonical_host(): check_target and host_matches_deny each had their own inline .lower().rstrip('.'), and a limiter with a different notion of identity would give 'a.com.' its own bucket and silently double the rate. Extraction verified behaviour-preserving by the 467 pre-existing tests. KNOWN LIMIT, stated in the class docstring: per-process only, so N workers means N budgets; a cross-process limit needs shared storage (P11).

tasks.title: Wire plan().recheck to the probe path via a claim/write-back protocol (ADR-038)
tasks.notes: Measured BEFORE writing: readers of .recheck/.recheck_ready = 1 each (both inside scheduler.py's own bucket sum); production writes of ProxyState.PROBING = 0; two consecutive passes selected the SAME row (3fd692f1f03a4fe8); naive write-back vs a live lease = CLOBBERED. The one-line version would have shipped a double-delivery: upsert_many sets EVERY column from a Proxy loaded before the lease existed, returning state=READY/lease_id=NULL under a live consumer. Critically, double_delivery_violations() returned [] on that clobber -- the P05 H3 audit reconstructs LEASE/RELEASE/EXPIRE from the append-only log and no second LEASE was ever appended. An audit that watches one mechanism is blind to a violation produced by another. After: lease_clobber NO OVERLAP, double_probe [], probing_absorbing returns to COOLING and re-enters the ADR-006 ladder.

tasks.title: Derive the claim lifetime from the real probe plan instead of a hand-picked literal (ADR-039)
tasks.notes: Measured BEFORE: probe_ms default 120000 vs 590000 required at batch 100/concurrency 10 -- short by 470000ms (~5x), and probe_ms=1 was accepted. The wave factor is what the old default missed: one claim covers the whole batch but a semaphore admits only `concurrency` at a time, so required = worst_case_per_probe * ceil(batch/concurrency). Raising the literal to 590000 was REJECTED as the fix: the next change to k, a timeout, or the ladder would make a new hand-picked number silently wrong again, which is that literal's entire history. PROTOCOL_LADDER moved to core and imported by the adapter so bound and priced code cannot disagree. claim_bound deliberately OVER-prices (75000/750000, all four rungs) because aiohttp-socks is absent so two rungs currently cost ~0; the test asserts equality when restricted to the measured rungs and strict excess otherwise -- pinning 590000 would have converted a safety margin into a regression the suite DEMANDED.

tasks.title: Count recheck abandonment inside the reclaiming UPDATE and bound it with its own retirement ladder
tasks.notes: Measured BEFORE: 12 crash cycles driven, consecutive_failures 0, total_attempts 0, ever retired false -- the abandon path was not merely unbounded, it was INVISIBLE. Counter incremented INSIDE the reclaiming UPDATE: atomic with PROBING->COOLING and idempotent because the state='PROBING' predicate means a second concurrent reclaim matches nothing. The caller cannot do it -- the abandoning worker is dead by definition (H8: SIGKILL is uncatchable). Counter is CONSECUTIVE, cleared by record_success AND record_failure: a probe that reported bad news is not abandoning its claim; a cumulative counter would retire a healthy proxy for unrelated crashes weeks apart. retire_after_abandoned_rechecks is a SEPARATE knob from retire_after_consecutive_failures because the two count different events. Expiry is inclusive (<=) to match expire_leases, verified by reading both methods' SQL rather than asserting my newer test's assumption. Evidence paths CORRECTED before the gate would pass: I first wrote retire_abandoned against core/policy/lifecycle.py and the claim method as claim_for_recheck; done_tasks_have_evidence resolves the symbol INSIDE the named file and refused both. retire_abandoned is a store method (the retirement is one UPDATE, not a pure decision) and the claim is claim_for_probe. The ADR-037 lesson holds: an evidence list that cannot be checked is the same defect as a Verify line naming nothing.

tasks.title: Level-6 E2E suite: a full cycle against a REAL SqliteStore populates a real pool, dedupes on cycle 2, and the scheduler drives recheck through the same store
tasks.notes: The level-6 suite is the first to wire DiscoveryEngine + SqliteStore + HandoutService + PoolScheduler together with no fakes. Three traps documented for the next writer: (1) pytest-asyncio is NOT installed, so bare 'async def test_' is collected, never awaited, and reported PASSED (ADR-010 vacuous pass) -- the runs_async decorator drives asyncio.run, and wrapper.__signature__ = inspect.signature(fn) is CRITICAL because pytest resolves fixtures from the collected signature, not from __wrapped__; the meta-test test_no_test_in_this_module_is_a_bare_coroutine asserts none survive; (2) the P07 RFC-5737 lesson recurred -- 203.0.113.x fixture IPs are non-global per ipaddress and the REAL normalizer silently dropped them, so fixtures use globally-routable ranges (45.10.20.x, 103.21.40.x, 185.220.101.x); (3) interface facts verified by reading source, not assuming: parse_body(parser: str, body: str) returns ParseResult.candidates; PoolScheduler.plan() takes no now arg (clock injected); CycleReport has no 'seen' attr; SourceStats field is last_reason; SqliteStore exposes count_by_state/select_schedulable, not ready_for_lease.

tasks.title: V4-03 found and fixed: intake dedup keys on the endpoint, never the fingerprint (ADR-040)
tasks.notes: REAL DEFECT, same seam class as V4-01/V4-02: unit tests could not see it because FakeStore.get and SqliteStore.get encoded the SAME wrong assumption (fingerprint identity == endpoint identity). fingerprint = sha256(endpoint|protocol); intake candidates are Protocol.UNKNOWN, stored rows carry the DISCOVERED protocol, so get(candidate.fingerprint) never matched and cycle 2 re-probed 8 of 10 known endpoints. Only the 2 TCP-refused rows were skipped -- rejected BEFORE discovery, stored under UNKNOWN, accidentally matching the intake key. Fix: store.get_by_endpoint(host, port) returns every stored row for that host:port across ALL protocols; process_source dedups on it. The fingerprint stays PRIMARY KEY for the lease protocol (H3) -- it was only ever wrong as a DEDUP key. FakeStore in test_engine.py was rewritten to hold real Proxy rows so the fake can no longer encode the defect. Verified: cycle 2 probes 0, skipped_known == 10, at unit AND real-store integration level.

invariant_notes.H3_no_double_delivery: EARNED 2026-08-24 (P05). Established by four independent mechanisms, because no single one suffices: (1) real process concurrency via multiprocessing/spawn, one parametrisation oversubscribed (48 requested from a pool of 24) -> 24 unique, 0 duplicates; (2) a COMMITTED negative control, NaiveStore's read-then-write lease, which the same assertion catches at 30 duplicates on an IDENTICAL config (pool 12, 6 procs x 6) where the real store gives 0 -- without this the green result would be indistinguishable from a test that never created contention; (3) an independent append-only lease_log audit, double_delivery_violations(), which examines what happened instead of asking lease() to report on itself; (4) AST guards on structure, since the correct and broken implementations are behaviourally identical single-threaded. Artifact: engineering/raw/lease_concurrency.json.
invariant_notes.H7_live_not_good: UPGRADED 2026-08-24 (P06): the k=1 caveat is RETIRED. The gate has now been applied to live proxies with real k=5 sampling (engineering/raw/admission_live_adr024.json): 300 probed, 86 tcp_ok, 12 reached the gate, 6 with 2+ samples, 3 ADMITTED. The rules the k=1 replay could not reach fired on real data: UNRELIABLE 2, TOO_SLOW_P95 2, NOT_MEASURED 5. Getting there required fixing two v4 defects the green suite hid: V4-01/ADR-025 (a measured cause overwritten by an untestable-SOCKS note, so 0 proxies reached the gate) and V4-02/ADR-024 (floor-rank p95 returned the MINIMUM at k=2, admitting a proxy measured over budget -- H7's own failure mode reintroduced through the estimator). TOO_JITTERY has still never fired live (0 of 6); it is proven by unit test only, and that is stated rather than papered over.
invariant_notes.H8_crash_resume: EARNED 2026-08-24 (P05). SQLite WAL + synchronous=FULL. A child process writes, prints an ACK, then os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGKILL); the parent asserts returncode == -9 (signal 9 is uncatchable, so no finally/atexit/context manager ran) and then reopens the db and finds every acknowledged row. Exports are .tmp + fsync + os.replace in the SAME directory, with the fsync-before-replace ORDER asserted by AST -- a reader never observes a truncated file.
